title: I made a PS1-style noir gun shop game with Claude: every texture and sound effect generated from code (free, plays in browser)
author: KometUnit1108
selftext:
\*\*CHAMBER SERVICE\*\* is a short PS1-style noir. You run a gun shop at night. Every customer wants a gun; some of them are cops, robbers or hired killers. Sell to the wrong person and the night ends badly. Shoot first and you'd better be right.



Play free in your browser: [https://wavedash.com/games/chamberservice](https://wavedash.com/games/chamberservice)



\*\*How it was made\*\*

I directed and playtested; Claude (Anthropic) did the building with me, conversation by conversation, in Godot 4.7.



\- \*\*Code:\*\* all GDScript: customer behaviour, night events (phone calls, radio news, patrol cars), 4 languages (EN/JA/RU/ES)

\- \*\*Textures:\*\* generated by a Python script, palette-reduced to look like 1997

\- \*\*Sound:\*\* every effect synthesized in Python. No samples at all

\- \*\*3D:\*\* the shop and the customers are built from code. The only outside assets are 3 low-poly gun models by TastyTony (Sketchfab, CC BY 4.0), recoloured to match

\- \*\*Look:\*\* low-res render + vertex snapping + dithering/grain post shader



\*\*What worked\*\*

\- \*\*Scripted autotests\*\* that drive the real game headless: \~50 scenarios, plus bots that play whole nights. They caught regressions after every change.

\- \*\*Real playtesters.\*\* First feedback: "everyone just shoots every customer." Instead of making it harder, we added consequences (the boss calls you, strikes, raids) and tells for reading people.

\- \*\*Second round:\*\* "it feels like fast-forward." Instead of speeding things up, we filled the quiet gaps with events: calls, radio news about guns you sold, patrol cars passing the window.



\*\*Gotcha if you ship Godot 4.x to the web\*\*

Our web build was completely silent. Godot's web export defaults to "Sample" audio playback, and in our case that meant no sound at all. Setting \`audio/general/default\_playback\_type.web\` to Stream fixed it.



Happy to answer questions about the workflow.

comments.author: KometUnit1108
comments.body:
Dev note: the most useful part of the whole process was the playtest loop. My friend's first reaction was "I just shoot every customer", so the fix wasn't harder customers, it was consequences plus readable tells (the hitman always wears black gloves).

Curious how others here handle playtesting when building with AI: do you script automated tests, rely on real players, or both?
